ready1_open_rewrite.title: SciVerse open question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: An experiment involving fruit flies produced the following results: 1) Wing phenotype: intact wings are the wild type, and crumpled wings are the mutant. 2) Body color phenotype: gray body color is dominant, and black body color is the mutant. Based on the above data, what genetic relationship is shown between the genes controlling wing phenotype and body color phenotype?

matched_variant_raw.title: SciVerse open question
matched_variant_raw.rewritten_question_text:
An experiment involving fruit flies produced the following results:

1) Wing phenotype: intact wings are the wild type, and crumpled wings are the mutant.
2) Body color phenotype: gray body color is dominant, and black body color is the mutant.

Based on the above data, what genetic relationship is shown between the genes controlling wing phenotype and body color phenotype?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: An experiment involving fruit flies produced the following results: 1) Wing phenotype: intact wings are the wild type, and crumpled wings are the mutant. 2) Body color phenotype: gray body color is dominant, and black body color is the mutant. Based on the above data, what genetic relationship is shown between the genes controlling wing phenotype and body color phenotype?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the left side of the image lists four types of fruit fly offspring phenotypes and numbers: 525 vestigial, gray-bodied flies; 555 crumpled, black-bodied flies; 75 crumpled, gray flies; 45 vestigial, black-bodied flies. The right side of the image gives the symbol correspondences: V = vestigial, v = crumpled, G = gray, g = black. Then reason: the question asks to determine the genetic relationship between the genes controlling wing phenotype and body color phenotype. Among the four types of offspring, the vestigial gray and crumpled black two types have very large numbers, while the crumpled gray and vestigial black two types have very small numbers. If the two genes assorted independently, the numbers of the four types of offspring should be roughly similar; now there is a pattern in which parental types are significantly more numerous and recombinant types are significantly fewer, indicating that the two genes do not assort independently but are linked on the same chromosome. Therefore the answer is linkage.
